# Fees and Deposits
This organisation is fictional.
Adopted on 12 February 2025; effective from 1 March 2025.

## 1 Paying at the desk
### 1.1 Payment methods
Pay in pounds by cash or card before collecting a loan.
The desk gives a receipt showing the payment date and what the payment covers.
### 1.2 No ordinary loan fee
There is no separate charge for an ordinary toy or tool loan.
Late, missing and damaged items are dealt with under lend-borrowing.md.

## 2 Annual membership
### 2.1 Standard annual fee
The annual household membership fee is £24 for each 12-month term.
The fee is payable on joining and on each renewal.
### 2.2 Reduced annual fee
The annual fee is £12 if either named adult declares that the household receives income support.
No benefit letter is required; record the declaration on the application.
The reduced fee cannot be combined with any other fee reduction.

## 3 Deposits and records
### 3.1 Tool deposit
Collect a refundable £20 deposit for each powered tool before handing it over.
No deposit is required for toys or hand tools.
Deposit deductions and repayment times are set out in lend-refunds.md.
### 3.2 Unpaid charges
An unpaid charge blocks new loans and renewal until paid or formally waived.
A pending appeal does not remove this block.
### 3.3 Approval of waivers
Only the committee may waive a charge, with the amount and reason recorded in its minutes.

# Borrowing Rules
This organisation is fictional.
Adopted on 12 February 2025; effective from 1 March 2025.

## 1 Taking items home
### 1.1 Household limit
A household may hold up to 4 items, including no more than 2 tools.
Each item with its own stock number counts as one item, even if it contains several pieces.
### 1.2 Eligibility
Membership must be active, and all charges must be paid or formally waived.
Powered tools also require the deposit in lend-fees.md and the handover in lend-safety.md.

## 2 Loan periods
### 2.1 Ordinary loan
An ordinary loan lasts 14 calendar days from its collection date.
The desk writes the due date on the receipt.
### 2.2 One extension
The desk may grant one extension of 7 calendar days if nobody has reserved the item.
Ask before the current due date; an overdue loan cannot be extended.
### 2.3 Closed return dates
If a due date falls when the desk is closed, return by the next advertised opening.
An extension runs from the recorded due date, including any closure adjustment.

## 3 Reservations and late returns
### 3.1 Reservations
Each household may reserve up to 2 items; collection is due within 7 days of notification.
### 3.2 Overdue charge
Charge £1 per item for each calendar day after its recorded due date, capped at £10 per item.
### 3.3 Missing items
After 28 days overdue, the committee may declare an item lost and apply lend-refunds.md.

# Front-Desk Quick Guide
This organisation is fictional.
Prepared on 2 June 2025; retained without updating on 8 August 2026.

## What this sheet is for
This is a reminder, not the rulebook, and some figures below are now out of date.
The governing documents prevail over this guide.
Apply any relevant replacement in lend-changes.md before giving a final answer.

## Joining
Membership is for local adults, with room for 2 adults from the same household.
Ask for a recent document showing the applicant's name and address.
The usual annual fee is £24, or £12 for a household declaring income support.
Membership runs for a year once approval and payment are complete.
Check lend-membership.md and lend-fees.md before accepting payment.

## Borrowing
A household can have 4 items, but only 2 of them can be tools.
Ordinary loans are for a fortnight, with one extra week if nobody is waiting.
Powered tools need a £20 deposit each and a first-time handover for the collecting adult.
Write down the actual due date, allowing for a closed desk.
Check lend-borrowing.md and lend-safety.md when booking the loan.

## Returns and problems
Late items cost £1 a day each, up to £10 each.
An unused first membership can be refunded if the request arrives within a week.
Tool deposits normally come back within a week of return and inspection.
Do not promise a refund or charge for damage without checking lend-refunds.md.
Record unsafe behaviour and use lend-conduct.md for complaints or suspensions.

**The overdue charge is £20, and they can't take the new toy until it's paid or formally waived.**

**Charge**
- Both items were due on 8 May 2026. By Monday 25 May they are 17 calendar days overdue (9 days left in May after the 8th, plus 8 days in the second half).
- Under lend-borrowing.md §3.2, the charge is £1 per item for each calendar day after the recorded due date, capped at £10 per item.
- At 17 days, each item hits the cap: £17 becomes £10.
- Two items at £10 each comes to **£20**.
- The 14-day versus 21-day loan period doesn't change this. Both items already have a recorded due date, and lend-changes.md doesn't alter the overdue charge.

**New toy**
- lend-borrowing.md §1.2 says all charges must be paid or formally waived before a household can borrow.
- lend-fees.md §3.2 says an unpaid charge blocks new loans until it is paid or formally waived. A pending appeal doesn't lift that block.
- Only the committee can waive a charge, and it must record the amount and reason in its minutes (lend-fees.md §3.3). Desk staff can't waive it.
- The household can pay the £20 at the desk (cash or card) on the same visit and then take out the new toy. Their membership must also be active, and they'd be within the 4-item limit once the two returns are processed.
